rows: Pāṇini's 14 Śiva Sūtra markers are metalinguistic operators with defined input, output, and class-changing semantics
The Sefer seam has no defined input, output, or class-changing semantics in the Sefer text
The Sefer 231 count is consistent with 22 letters + 0 operators; inconsistent with 23 ordinary letters
Pāṇini's system generates 305 theoretical pratyāhāras; ~43 used
Sanskrit attests the geocentric planetary order as a third independent witness
The Marcosian planet-by-vowel mapping remains interpretive; Sanskrit does not resolve it
Sanskrit's 5×5 stop matrix maps partially onto the Hebrew 22; gutturals and liquids have no Sanskrit stop equivalent
The 43 count in Pāṇini and the Sri Yantra is a structural coincidence, not a forced generative law
The $T(i)=8-i$ reversal is conditional on the geocentric interpretation of the Marcosian heavens
Sanskrit provides an independent phonetic reference for the stop/affricate portion of the Hebrew 22, but not for gutturals/liquids
